issuer: the Alaska Division of Motor Vehicles
note: The Alaska Statutes on akleg.gov (read 2026-10-30): AS 28.15 sets each noncommercial licence fee at $20 (a skills test $15 more, not held) and has a licence expire on the birthday in the eighth year after issue; AS 28.15.057 lets someone 16 or 17 have a (full) driver's licence only after six months on an instruction permit and six on a provisional licence, so a full licence is kept from 17 (16½ rounded up). AS 18.65.310 issues an identification card for $15; its term isn't stated there, so it is null. The DMV's own pages refused the request behind a captcha.

sources.title: Alaska Statutes, AS 28.15 (Drivers' Licenses)
sources.said: (1) all noncommercial vehicles and motor-driven cycles (A) each license fee ..... $20; ... a driver's license expires on the licensee's birthday in the eighth year following the issuance of a new license ... a person who is at least 16 years of age but not yet 18 years of age may not be issued a driver's license unless the person has (1) been licensed under an instruction permit ... (2) held a valid provisional driver's license issued under AS 28.15.055 for at least six months;

sources.title: Alaska Statutes, AS 18.65.310 (Identification cards)
sources.said: Upon payment of a $15 fee, the department shall issue a card identical to the motor vehicle operator's license
